raw_response:
I am already committed to the wheat-maize rotation on most of my land, because on a small place like 7.7 mu I cannot gamble too much. Wheat gives me one steady harvest, then maize follows quickly, and that spreads the risk better than putting everything into one crop. But I still keep some cotton because I have grown it many years, I know how to manage it, and if the weather is decent it gives me cash. I have studied enough to pay attention to rates and timing, but after 40 years I still trust what my own fields tell me more than anything. This year I will keep the wheat-maize system on 5 mu and put 2.7 mu into cotton. For wheat, since it is already in the field, I will not chase yield blindly. I will topdress once around jointing, watch leaf color, and irrigate carefully because well water costs money. After wheat harvest I will move fast into summer maize with simple tillage so I do not miss moisture or planting time. Cotton takes more management and picking labor, so I keep it on a smaller area that the family can still handle.
